answer: Kernel churn tax forces each new identity to pay a fee equal to the cumulative fees of all prior identities registered from the same device fingerprint. At zenith of the curve, a 1,000-clone attacker pays the sum of 1,000 prior fees before the 1,001st identity can transact. Each clone also enters a 48-hour reef window with zero transaction access, so mass sybil creation yields no immediate utility.
